Estimate the light on sensors and cells from a precomputed geometry

Source: R/estimate_pacl_from_geometry.R
estimate_pacl_from_geometry.Rd

Estimates the light reaching the sensors and cells of a stand for given crown leaf area densities (turbid medium) or crown openness (porous envelope), from the geometry computed by precompute_sl_geometry. Results are the same as the sensors and cells outputs of run_sl_advanced with the same settings (up to rounding errors), but much faster, since the rays are not traced again. The light intercepted by trees cannot be estimated from the geometry.

Usage

estimate_pacl_from_geometry(
  sl_geometry,
  trees,
  turbid_medium = TRUE,
  extinction_coef = 0.5,
  clumping_factor = 1,
  trunk_interception = TRUE,
  detailed_output = FALSE
)

Arguments

sl_geometry

An object of class "sl_geometry" created by precompute_sl_geometry.

trees

A data frame with one row per tree of the stand used to compute the geometry, with the column id_tree, and the column crown_lad (if turbid_medium = TRUE) or crown_openness (if turbid_medium = FALSE), as in sl_stand$trees. Other columns are ignored, and the order of the rows does not matter (trees are matched by id_tree).

turbid_medium

Logical. If TRUE, crowns are represented as turbid media using crown_lad. If FALSE, crowns are represented as porous envelopes using crown_openess. Defaults to TRUE.

extinction_coef

Numeric scalar. Leaf extinction coefficient controlling the attenuation of radiation by foliage. It represents the effective light attenuation per unit leaf area and is related to average leaf orientation. Higher values increase light interception. Defaults to 0.5.

clumping_factor

Numeric scalar controlling the aggregation of foliage within the crown volume. A value of 1 corresponds to homogeneous foliage distribution, values below 1 indicate clumped foliage, and values above 1 indicate more regular spacing. This parameter affects light interception in the turbid-medium model. Defaults to 1.

trunk_interception

Logical. If TRUE, account for interception by tree trunks. Defaults to TRUE.

detailed_output

Logical. If TRUE, retain detailed ray, energy, and interception information, including the monthly ray discretization and interception matrices. If FALSE, only the main light-interception metrics are returned. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

A list with two data frames, sensors and cells, with the same columns as in the output of run_sl_advanced (light$sensors and light$cells): id_sensor or id_cell, e, pacl and punobs, and their direct and diffuse components if detailed_output = TRUE. As in run_sl_advanced, energies are on a horizontal plane for sensors and on the slope plane for cells. A data frame is empty if the geometry toward these targets was not computed.

Details

For each ray toward each target, the energy reaching the target is the energy of the ray above the canopy times the transmittance of the crossed crowns: \(\exp(-k \Omega \sum LAD \times length)\) for turbid media, or the product of the crown openness for porous envelopes. It is null if a trunk intercepts the ray and trunk_interception = TRUE.

See also

precompute_sl_geometry, run_sl_advanced

Examples

data_prenovel <- SamsaRaLight::data_prenovel

stand <- create_sl_stand(
  trees_inv = data_prenovel$trees,
  cell_size = 10,
  latitude = data_prenovel$info$latitude,
  slope = data_prenovel$info$slope,
  aspect = data_prenovel$info$aspect,
  north2x = data_prenovel$info$north2x
)
#> SamsaRaLight stand successfully created.

geometry <- precompute_sl_geometry(
  sl_stand = stand,
  monthly_radiations = data_prenovel$radiations
)
#> parallel mode: DISABLED | Threads = 1 (user) | Cores available = 4
#> SamsaRaLight geometry was computed successfully.

# Light on the cells for two crown LAD values
trees <- stand$trees

trees$crown_lad <- 0.5
head(estimate_pacl_from_geometry(geometry, trees)$cells)
#>   id_cell        e      pacl    punobs
#> 1       1 480.4950 0.1059478 0.1993924
#> 2       2 725.7215 0.1600196 0.4950759
#> 3       3 982.0738 0.2165446 0.7438652
#> 4       4 695.8185 0.1534261 0.5863522
#> 5       5 693.4853 0.1529116 0.2809002
#> 6       6 481.9791 0.1062751 0.5764287

trees$crown_lad <- 1
head(estimate_pacl_from_geometry(geometry, trees)$cells)
#>   id_cell        e       pacl    punobs
#> 1       1 269.1524 0.05934738 0.3559582
#> 2       2 516.1033 0.11379937 0.6961536
#> 3       3 830.7490 0.18317789 0.8793638
#> 4       4 516.0327 0.11378381 0.7906373
#> 5       5 451.4412 0.09954156 0.4315072
#> 6       6 348.3622 0.07681291 0.7975221
